# Importing the Data

We are importing the LA Metro ridership dataset.

```{r}
metro <- read.csv("metro_ridership (1).csv")

head(metro)›

```
```{r}
# Check the variables & data types
str(metro)

#View basic statistics of each variable
summary(metro)

# Count the missing values in each column
colSums(is.na(metro))
```
```{r}
# Checking for repeated records (same line, year, or month)
sum(duplicated(metro[c("line_name", "year", "month")]))

```

## Checking for values that are unusual
```{r}
# Some zeros might mean the line isn't running / data isn't being recorded

# Zero values for weekdays
sum(metro$est_wkday_ridership == 0)

# Zero values for Saturday 
sum(metro$est_sat_ridership == 0)

# Zero values for Sunday 
sum(metro$est_sun_ridership == 0)

#Ridership should not be negative, so I am checking that as well

# Negative weekdays
sum(metro$est_wkday_ridership < 0)

# Negative Saturdays
sum(metro$est_sat_ridership < 0)

# Negative Sundays
sum(metro$est_sun_ridership < 0)
```
```{r}
# To check which lines have zero weekday ridership
table(metro$line_name[metro$est_wkday_ridership == 0])
```

## Now creating a data column, preparing the data

```{r}

# Putting the year and month together, so we can use the dates for graphs
metro$date <- as.Date(paste(metro$year, metro$month, "01", sep="-"))

# Checking if the dates worked
head(metro$date)

```
